sources.title: Tape Notes 188: Tame Impala — My Old Ways and Loser
sources.coverage: Complete automatic speech transcript reviewed for production content; no full human audio audit.
sources.notes: ASR can mishear names and speaker turns. Times match an 81:23 ad-supported copy accessed 2026-09-08; dynamic advertisements can shift player offsets. Source claims are paraphrased. Song performances and advertisements excluded.

claims.title: Keep the first spark
claims.claim: A short spontaneous demo became the foundation of the record; Parker kept its first section rather than replacing every rough detail.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: A song can outgrow its initial destination
claims.claim: He initially considered the idea unsuitable for Tame Impala and considered giving it to Mark Ronson, before deciding to keep it.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Guitar controller opens unfamiliar sounds
claims.claim: The opening instrumental demo used a Strat with a taped-on synth pickup and a Roland guitar synthesizer; he tentatively recalls the GR-55 model.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: The famous bass begins as guitar
claims.claim: The riff uses a modeled P-bass sound played on guitar and shifted into the bass register, then processed. This is not proof that the entire song contains no bass guitar.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Overdrive recollection is tentative
claims.claim: He thinks Ableton Overdrive shaped the synthesized bass and demonstrates something similar; the original exact preset and stereo treatment are not recovered.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Leave useful mistakes in
claims.claim: The rough original performance contains small mistakes, which did not prevent it becoming the final foundation.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Reuse a recorded drum idea
claims.claim: He reused a drum recording made weeks earlier and thinks it was recorded outside; he wanted a controlled, dry contrast to Lonerism room wash.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Reinforce the acoustic loop
claims.claim: An 808 kick and Sequential Circuits Drumtraks were added later to the original drum recording.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Return later with a different palette
claims.claim: The later section was developed much later in another studio, using keyboards that were then available; the arrangement changes with that palette.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Preserve the Greco correction
claims.claim: For a later bass part he first says Hofner, then corrects himself to Greco. Do not turn the initial slip into a definitive Hofner attribution.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Performance before a preamp upgrade
claims.claim: Parker emphasizes playing and listening over premium preamps, recalling a relatively inexpensive PreSonus rack unit without confidently naming its model.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Reduce sympathetic ringing at the kit
claims.claim: He names a Ludwig Supraphonic 400 snare and Tama kick and describes removing toms to reduce unwanted resonance.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Separate this setup from other bedrooms
claims.claim: Duvets describe a bedroom method, whereas he recalls this particular take as outdoors. These are alternatives, not one combined recording setup.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Work with imperfect microphone capture
claims.claim: He recalls a borrowed vocal microphone on kick, a 57 beside the snare and another microphone above; the borrowed microphone model is unidentified.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Compression supplies the knock
claims.claim: The dbx 165 was central to his drum character across several albums. Its envelope mattered; a single owned unit encouraged mono processing.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Do not invent the distortion stage
claims.claim: Asked about distortion following the compressor, he is uncertain. The available discussion does not establish a fixed distortion chain.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Unprinted outboard complicates recall
claims.claim: He describes not having printed the outboard drum sound and needing the hardware running at final mix time. The recall difficulty is explicit; printing stems is an editorial practical implication.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Editing is part of the performance
claims.claim: He layers drum-machine reinforcement and trims the loop, then questions its exact length. No exact universal bar count is established.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Layering kicks changes phase and feel
claims.claim: Aligning the added kick with the original drum recording proved troublesome; the discussion concerns timing and phase rather than a fixed recipe.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Hi-hat placement gives the loop feel
claims.claim: He describes hi-hats sitting slightly behind the beat. No millisecond offset or swing percentage is supplied.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Judge the interacting envelopes
claims.claim: Kick and snare interaction is fundamental to the groove; detailed editing is a musical skill, and reproducing that recorded feel live remained difficult.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Keep the microphone recollection qualified
claims.claim: He recalls an SM7-family microphone and possibly the PreSonus preamp, probably without compression during tracking. This is a Currents recollection, not his later Deadbeat chain.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Shure mixer belongs to the drum discussion
claims.claim: The beige Shure compressor-mixer is mentioned for many Currents drum sounds; that aside does not establish its use on this vocal track. Publisher tags identify SE-30.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Doubles without assumed harmonies
claims.claim: Parker recalls double-tracked vocals and thinks there were no harmonies on the part under discussion.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Old delay naming is uncertain
claims.claim: He cycles through Ableton delay names while remembering an old session. Do not claim the modern Echo device was used on a 2015 recording from this recollection alone.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Likely reverb and dynamics
claims.claim: He tentatively identifies Waves RVerb, possibly Ableton Compressor, and Ableton multiband processing. Exact settings are not supplied.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Automate the throws
claims.claim: Delay and reverb throws supplied much of the vocal movement; his retrospective criticism is that the vocals were too low and reverberant.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Monitor for a comfortable performance
claims.claim: He describes tracking with one headphone ear off and monitoring through the interface rather than hearing DAW effects; Lynx Aurora is a tentative recollection.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Tight doubles still contain difference
claims.claim: Similar rhythmic phrasing with small natural pitch differences creates the vocal shimmer. No detuning amount or artificial delay setting is given.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Kronos supplies the later section
claims.claim: He identifies Korg Kronos as the main keyboard for the section after roughly the first minute and says it became a recurring instrument from Currents onward.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Keep the JV-1080 uncertainty
claims.claim: He mentions a Roland JV-1080 or similar module but does not confidently identify every part; he thinks the Rhodes-style sound was probably Kronos.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Layer without elaborate transitions
claims.claim: He describes the layered keyboard arrangement as relatively straightforward, with less elaborate transition processing than might be assumed.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Finishing and spontaneity coexist
claims.claim: Completing the later section gave a beloved demo a satisfying destination. His account values both quick invention and patience in finishing.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: The summing experiment was abandoned
claims.claim: He tried two passive Folcrom summing units feeding Neve preamps, but disliked attempted clipping and could not hear a meaningful summing improvement; cabling and latency added complexity.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Distinguish summing from stereo processing
claims.claim: After abandoning multichannel summing, he retained a stereo hardware route involving SPL Vitalizer and paired Neve 1073 stages, returning to Ableton for limiting.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: The bus compressor is unresolved
claims.claim: Parker tentatively recalls an SSL 500-series G compressor here. Sound On Sound separately names a Manley Variable Mu in publisher narration; these are not a verified combined serial chain.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Know the room you actually use
claims.claim: He describes Yamaha HS7 monitors without a subwoofer, four acoustic panels and a small bedroom. These are his working conditions, not a universal room-design prescription.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Use another trusted listening context
claims.claim: A trusted mastering friend in a larger room helped check the mix, including low-frequency balance around 100 Hz. The caption does not establish a reliable second monitor model.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Song structure can resist expectations
claims.claim: Parker discusses the unconventional chorus return and section layout. His offhand release chronology is not used here as verified historical dating.
claims.era: Currents / The Less I Know the Better

claims.title: Record before working the idea out
claims.claim: He records a phone memo while learning an idea so that the act of playing it does not overwrite the original thought.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Recreate the room, keep the intention
claims.claim: My Old Ways begins with a re-recorded living-room piano, not the initial memo. He wanted a stereo version that preserved the intimate perspective.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Reference another finished mix
claims.claim: He places reference audio such as Dua Lipa’s Levitating in the session to regain perspective while working alone.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: A smaller electronic drum palette
claims.claim: The Deadbeat foundation combines an 808 through a guitar amp with a Vermona DRM1, synchronized and recorded in different ways. No amp model or fixed settings are given.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Make the repeating bar convincing
claims.claim: He describes electronic grooves as a challenge of making a short repeating pattern danceable, with tiny percussion placements and gradual changes maintaining movement.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Do not import every acoustic habit
claims.claim: Electronic beats need not inherit a drummer’s automatic continuous eighth-note hi-hat pattern; he deliberately questions those habits.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Protect a simple foundation
claims.claim: For My Old Ways he resisted automatically building a dense arrangement, preserving the piano riff and drums as its identity.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Make the form express the subject
claims.claim: The returning musical pattern and rising, increasingly chaotic synth parts support the song’s theme of falling back into old behavior.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Comfort determines the microphone
claims.claim: He values holding the microphone; a U47-style clone sounded good but did not suit that performance habit. He corrects an initial SM57 reference to SM7.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Amp treatment appears on Deadbeat
claims.claim: He describes routing vocals through guitar amplification, sometimes singing into a microphone connected to the amp; End of Summer is his example. The surrounding SM57/SM7 correction makes its exact microphone uncertain.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Track through the familiar compressor
claims.claim: He now records vocals through his old dbx 165, previously used on early-album drums, and may add further compression and EQ in the session.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: A single hook contrasts with doubled verses
claims.claim: On My Old Ways he keeps the central hook single to suggest a sampled phrase, while the verses are doubled.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Whisper takes add width
claims.claim: Two more whispery takes sit hard left and right around the more central vocal double. The side layers are filtered and heavily compressed; exact cutoffs and ratios are unstated.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Separate vocal effects bus
claims.claim: He describes a separate effects bus on Deadbeat and names Soundtoys EchoBoy for its stereo character and Valhalla Room among the vocal effects.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Spring reverb device name needs care
claims.claim: He describes an Ableton convolution spring reverb used on most tracks, correcting his own initial spring-echo wording. The exact device version or impulse response is not established.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs
gear: Ableton convolution spring reverb (exact device unspecified)

claims.title: Decapitator adds occasional grit
claims.claim: He names Decapitator on vocals for songs including Dracula. He does not provide a mode, drive value or mix setting.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: A primitive lead among electronic repetition
claims.claim: He tentatively identifies the My Old Ways solo as Roland SH-1, valuing a meandering organ-like performance against the sequenced backdrop.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Room sound closes the loop
claims.claim: The sound of getting off the piano stool at the end intentionally answers the opening arrival at the piano.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Direction matters, but audition the idea
claims.claim: He admires a producer’s ability to hear what a song needs to reach completion, while emphasizing that results remain unknown until tried.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: What Fridmann demonstrated
claims.claim: He identifies saturation, compression that retains dynamics, and reverb that does not wash out the mix as lessons from working with Dave Fridmann as mixer. No exact settings are supplied.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Loser used a different recording method
claims.claim: The song largely retained its studio multitracking to tape, beginning with a complete drum performance and layering instruments afterward, with very little looping.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Full takes carry pressure and imperfections
claims.claim: He describes tape-recording anxiety, stick clicks and other retained performance details. He later recalls a click printed to tape, so this should not be reported as definitely click-free.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: The decisive word can arrive last
claims.claim: Loser was the final lyric word selected, after trying alternatives against its rhythmic space; he connects an alternative word with the album title in a tentative real-time recollection.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: A familiar synth anchors the record
claims.claim: He calls Prophet-5 central to Dracula and recurring sounds across Deadbeat, stressing that it was conveniently beside him rather than uniquely necessary equipment.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs

claims.title: Make the experiment before rejecting it
claims.claim: He advises starting more songs and testing melodies instead of assuming their quality in advance.
claims.era: Deadbeat / My Old Ways, Loser and related songs
